narrative.title: The Conveyor Re-rack to a Single Lane
narrative.scenario: A distribution hub is switching from a tree of branch conveyors to one straight express lane. Every station must survive the re-rack, and the order along the new lane must be exactly the hub-first walk of the old tree — each station's left spur is dismantled and spliced into the lane ahead of its right spur, all rewiring done with the existing stations and zero spare parts.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child).
narrative.outputFormat: Return the station values along the flattened lane — the preorder sequence after rewiring every left pointer to null and every right pointer to the next station.
constraints: Expected extra space: O(1) — flatten in place

testCases.explanation: The preorder walk 1-2-3-4-5-6 becomes the single right-leaning lane.
The left spur of node 2 splices in before nothing, so the lane keeps 1-2-3.

hintLevels: Level 1: The final lane is exactly the preorder sequence — the question is only how to rewire without extra storage.
Level 2: At each node, hang the right subtree off the left subtree's rightmost descendant, then lift the left subtree into the right slot.
Level 3: Advance one right-step at a time; every node is visited a bounded number of times, so it stays linear.
